test.title: Mini-test · A city learns to live with floods

paragraphs.text: When the river burst its banks in 2014, more than 3,000 homes in the city of Marbury were flooded. Many residents were unable to return for over a year, and small businesses in the old town suffered the greatest losses.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The city’s first response was to build higher walls along the river. The walls protected the centre during the next major flood in 2019, but water was pushed downstream, where two villages were flooded for the first time.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: This led the regional authority to change its approach. Instead of only building walls, it bought farmland upstream and allowed it to flood during storms, storing water that would otherwise reach the city.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Inside the city, new rules require that the ground floors of new buildings be used for garages, shops or storage rather than bedrooms. Existing homeowners can receive grants to install waterproof doors and to move electrical sockets higher up the walls.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Residents’ attitudes have also changed. A survey found that the share of households with a flood plan rose from one in ten before 2014 to more than half today. The city now sends text warnings to anyone who registers.
paragraphs.label: E
